notes:
Segment covers Bihar (st-br), Jharkhand (st-jh), Odisha (st-od) in full except districts (owned by local-lgd) and the High Courts serving them (owned by judiciary — Patna HC, Jharkhand HC, Orissa HC referenced by id only, not defined here).

Sourcing: primarily current-revision Wikipedia (fetched 2026-09-25 via the MediaWiki parse API and category-member API, under heavy shared rate-limiting from parallel sibling research agents on the same session — all fetches eventually succeeded after backoff) plus the state government infobox pages ("Government of Bihar/Jharkhand/Odisha") which proved to be reliable single-source aggregators for Speaker/Chief Secretary, and dedicated "<X> Police" pages for DGP names. WebSearch was unavailable for this segment (the shared 200-call session budget was exhausted by other parallel agents before this segment started); no browser tools were used or available; the source video file referenced in the original chat request was not accessible to this subagent and was not used.

KNOWN GAPS / LOW CONFIDENCE (do not treat these as verified):
1. Exact "since" dates are missing (null) for: all three states' Speaker (except Odisha), Chief Secretary, DGP, State Election Commissioner, PSC Chairman, Lokayukta, SHRC Chair/Chairperson — Wikipedia infoboxes and agency pages that named these office-holders did not give appointment dates; a 2025-2026 dated PIB/gazette source would be needed to fill these in.
2. Odisha Public Service Commission (OPSC) Chairman: could not find a current, individually-named chair anywhere in the fetched material; position included as vacant-unknown (confidence low) rather than guessed. Needs a direct opsc.gov.in check.
3. Bihar/Jharkhand/Odisha Lokayukta and Human Rights Commission holders are sourced only to each body's own Wikipedia infobox ("Agency executive" field), which is not dated — treat these names as confidence:low pending a 2025-2026 cross-check; Odisha SHRC chair is explicitly marked "Acting" on its own page.
4. Jharkhand Deputy Speaker: the Jharkhand_Legislative_Assembly infobox lists no Deputy Speaker at all as of the page's last edit — recorded here as vacant, but this could equally be a stale/incomplete infobox; unresolved.
5. Jharkhand Council of Ministers: one portfolio (Urban Development and Housing; Higher and Technical Education; Tourism, Arts, Culture, Sports & Youth Affairs), formerly held by Sudivya Kumar (JMM, Giridih), is vacant following his death on 6 September 2026 — only 19 days before this segment's as-of date; a reshuffle to fill it may already have happened and not yet be reflected on Wikipedia. Recorded as a vacant minister position (st-jh-pos-minister-10) rather than guessing a successor.
6. Bihar's 32 rank-and-file ministers (st-br-pos-minister-1..32) and Odisha's 13 (st-od-pos-minister-1..13, split cabinet/MoS-IC) have name+party+portfolio+since confirmed from each state's dedicated "<Name> ministry" Wikipedia article (a specific, tabulated, sourced page), but individual constituencies and personal Wikipedia links were NOT individually verified for the rank-and-file (non-CM/Deputy-CM) ministers — confidence:medium, wikipedia field left null rather than guessed, to respect the "never invent a URL" rule.
7. Municipal corporations: lists were built from Wikipedia's "Category:Municipal corporations in <state>" API plus targeted existence checks (Bihar Sharif, Saharsa, Jamshedpur, Berhampur, Sambalpur confirmed to exist as separate Municipal Corporation entities beyond the category listing; Puri and Bokaro checked and found NOT to be Municipal Corporations — Puri is a Municipality, Bokaro is administered differently). These lists (15 for Bihar, 9 for Jharkhand, 5 for Odisha) are believed complete as of the source but were not cross-checked against each state's Urban Development Department portal; mayors/commissioners were not looked up (task said "only if easily verifiable" — time did not allow).
8. Population figures: population2011 fields are the 2011 Census figures (verified in Bihar's case directly from body text: "At the 2011 census... 104,099,452"; Jharkhand and Odisha infobox population figures matched known 2011 census totals). Bihar's Wikipedia infobox headline population field actually shows a later (2023) projection (130,725,310), not 2011 — this segment correctly used the 2011 figure per the schema field name.
9. Odisha Assembly current party strength (BJP 79, BJD 50, INC 14, IND 3, CPI(M) 1 = 147) is taken from the Odisha Legislative Assembly infobox (which reflects post-election changes, e.g. independents joining BJP) rather than the original 2024 election-night result (BJP 78, BJD 51, INC 14, CPI(M) 1, IND 3); both are internally consistent (147 total) and the discrepancy is noted here for transparency.
10. Legislative Councils: only Bihar has one (Vidhan Parishad) among these three states; Jharkhand and Odisha are correctly modelled as unicameral.
11. High Courts (Patna, Jharkhand, Orissa) and their Chief Justices are judiciary-segment-owned and were only referenced by name in passing (not defined as entities/positions here).


ADVERSARIAL VERIFICATION PASS (2026-09-25): Re-checked 67 positions/facts against fresh Wikipedia fetches (MediaWiki parse API where reachable, WebFetch elsewhere after the API hit shared rate limits). 17 positions corrected (see top-level 'verification.corrections'), most significantly: Bihar Lokayukta was recorded under the wrong name ('Kirti Chandra Saha') — corrected to the actual current holder, Justice Sanjay Kumar Singh (since 2024-07-10). 5 municipal corporations were missing and have been added: Bettiah, Motihari, Samastipur, Sasaram (Bihar — the state has 19 MCs, not 15) and Puri (Odisha — upgraded to Municipal Corporation status after the original agent checked it). Two positions (Jharkhand Lokayukta, Jharkhand SHRC Chairperson) carry new notes flagging that their sole source (Wikipedia) is either stale (term expired years ago with no visible successor) or internally self-contradictory (names the holder as another state's commission chair in body text) — holders were kept rather than removed since a name is still the best available signal, but confidence stays low and these should not be treated as verified. Odisha's State Election Commissioner entry was downgraded to low confidence: the only available source conflates the State Election Commissioner (Article 243K body, this segment's proper subject) with the separate, ECI-linked Chief Electoral Officer post, and the stated 2019 appointment's 5-year term would already have lapsed.

entities.name: Bihar
entities.description: A state in eastern India, India's second most populous state (2011 census) and its most densely populated large state; capital Patna. Governed under the standard Governor–Council of Ministers model with a bicameral legislature (Assembly + Legislative Council).
